curriculum.title: Detailed Curriculum Details
curriculum.subtitle: Click on each level to explore the technical focus, software tools, and suggested practical projects.

level1.title: Level 1: Basic – Introduction and Shapes
level1.software: Tinkercad / Tinkercad Classrooms (Intuitive, secure, and free web tool)
level1.learn1: Spatial logic: Working plane comprehension, X, Y, Z axes, and basic shape alignment.
level1.learn2: Boolean operations: Grouping shapes to add volumes and create hollows (subtraction).
level1.learn3: Manufacturing concepts: What a 3D printer is, how plastic (PLA) melts, and the importance of gravity (overhangs).
level1.learn4: Basic preparation (Slicing): Introduction to Cura or PrusaSlicer to see how designs turn into layers.
level1.project: Design a nameplate with raised text, a custom keychain, or a geometric cookie cutter.
level1.focus: Basic geometry and printing plane logic.

level2.title: Level 2: Intermediate – Initial Technical & Parametric Design
level2.software: Onshape (free web tool for education, powerful and compatible with any computer or tablet) or Autodesk Fusion 360 (if school computers have good performance).
level2.learn1: 2D to 3D thinking: Sketch concepts, use of dimensions (exact measurements), and geometric constraints.
level2.learn2: Mechanical operations: Extrusion, revolution, shell, and fillets.
level2.learn3: Simple assembly design: Creating two separate parts that must fit together perfectly (print tolerances).
level2.learn4: Advanced slicing: Optimization of supports, infill patterns based on part use (aesthetic vs. functional), and layer heights.
level2.project: Design a mechanical articulated keychain, a phone stand with adjustable angle, or a box with a sliding lid.
level2.focus: Use of measurements, assemblies, and mechanical tolerances.

level3.title: Level 3: Advanced – Organic Modeling, Digital Sculpting & Real Applications
level3.software: Nomad Sculpt (fantastic if the school has iPads/tablets and styluses) or Blender (free for PC, with a steeper but professional learning curve).
level3.learn1: Digital sculpting: Using virtual brushes to stretch, inflate, flatten, and detail complex shapes.
level3.learn2: Organic geometry: Modeling fluid shapes, curves, and textures (animals, characters, prosthetics).
level3.learn3: Digitization & References: Working from outlines, plans, or scaled photographs to trace or adapt designs to reality.
level3.learn4: Maintenance & materials: Introduction to different types of filaments (PLA, PETG, flexible TPU) and troubleshooting common printer issues (clogs, bed calibration).
level3.project: Design an articulated fantasy creature, an ergonomic tool housing, or a simplified anatomical/medical model (like a splint or conceptual prosthesis for a pet or human).

level4.title: Level 4: Expert – Project Engineering, Manufacturing & Portfolio
level4.software: Combination of the above (Onshape/Fusion 360 + advanced slicers like Bambu Studio or PrusaSlicer to learn advanced slicing functions).
level4.learn1: Reverse engineering: Taking a broken or existing object, measuring it with calipers/rulers, and replicating or improving it in 3D.
level4.learn2: Manufacturing optimization: Designing for 3D printing (avoiding unnecessary supports, orienting parts for strength).
level4.learn3: Post-processing: Sanding, painting, joining large parts, and assembly with external elements (screws, magnets, LED lights).
level4.learn4: Project presentation: How to document the technical process, render designs, and pitch ideas.
level4.project: A free project with a social or technological basis. For example: automating a simple mechanism, designing safety solutions/shields for school labs, or creating a functional prototype for a school enterprise.
level4.focus: Reverse engineering, post-processing, and final project.

Reverse engineering, post-processing and final project.
